```{r}
#| label: trial-schematic-get-libraries

library(brms)
```

```{r}
#| label: trial-schematic-get-model
#| include: false

# -- response-accuracy core model (study/participant/text/question random intercepts)
dev.all.studies.noratings.ptqs.normal.0.1.normal.0.1.lkj.2.study.ri <- readRDS(
  "dev.all.studies.noratings.ptqs.normal.0.1.normal.0.1.lkj.2.study.ri.rds"
)

# -- core ratings model (study/participant/text random intercepts; no
# question-level grouping factor exists for ratings)
dev.ord.rating.all.studies.pts.normal.0.1.normal.0.1.lkj.2.study.ri.ad95 <- readRDS(
  "dev.ord.rating.all.studies.pts.normal.0.1.normal.0.1.lkj.2.study.ri.ad95.rds"
)
```

```{r}
#| label: trial-schematic-get-raw-data
#| include: false

# -- only the columns needed for raw per-unit mean response accuracy/rating
trial_schematic_data <- read_csv(
  "2026-06-17-all-studies-prog-DECISION-noNAs-tidy.csv",
  col_types = cols_only(
    ResponseId = col_factor(),
    study = col_factor(),
    text.id = col_factor(),
    text.question.id = col_factor(),
    response = col_double(),
    rating = col_double()
  )
)

# -- collapse to one row per participant x text for the ratings outcome
# (rating is recorded once per participant per text, not once per question)
trial_schematic_ratings_data <- trial_schematic_data %>%
  distinct(ResponseId, text.id, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  filter(!is.na(rating))
```

```{tikz}
    % Likelihood and linear predictor, combined on one line
    {\huge
    \begin{flalign*}
      &\mathrm{response}_i \sim \mathrm{Bernoulli}(p_i), \quad
         \operatorname{logit}(p_i)
         = \underbrace{\alpha + \bm{\beta}^\top\mathbf{x}_i}_{\text{fixed effects}}
         + \underbrace{u_{s[i]}}_{\substack{\text{study}\\\text{intercept}}}
         + \underbrace{\mathbf{v}_{j[i]}^\top\mathbf{t}_i}_{\substack{\text{participant intercept}\\\text{\&\ slopes}}}
         + \underbrace{\mathbf{w}_{t[i]}^\top\mathbf{p}_i}_{\substack{\text{text intercept}\\\text{\&\ slopes}}}
         + \underbrace{\mathbf{z}_{q[i]}^\top\mathbf{p}_i}_{\substack{\text{question intercept}\\\text{\&\ slopes}}}
      &
    \end{flalign*}
    }
    \vspace{8pt}
    {\LARGE
      $\mathbf{t}_i$: text features \& intercept (dim~6);\enspace
      $\mathbf{p}_i$: participant features, interactions \& intercept (dim~7)}
    \end{minipage}%
  };

\end{tikzpicture}
```

```{r}
#| label: trial-schematic-overlay-helpers
#| include: false

# -- raw per-unit means as a bottom grey layer, model-estimated random
# intercepts (already converted to the outcome's natural scale by the
# caller) as an upper coloured layer. `panel_title = NULL` omits the
# per-panel title entirely (used by the composite figure below, which
# labels each panel via its x-axis instead and gives the whole grid one
# shared title).
make_overlay_hist <- function(raw_df, model_df, fill_values, panel_title = NULL,
                               xlab, binwidth, xlim_range = NULL, xbreaks = NULL,
                               xlabels = NULL) {
  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_histogram(data = raw_df, aes(x = mean, fill = "Raw mean"),
                    binwidth = binwidth, alpha = 0.6, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
    geom_histogram(data = model_df, aes(x = mean, fill = "Model estimate"),
                    binwidth = binwidth, alpha = 0.6, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = fill_values, name = NULL) +
    labs(x = xlab, y = "Count") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 9))
  if (!is.null(panel_title) && nzchar(panel_title)) {
    p <- p + labs(title = panel_title)
  }
  # -- always show the outcome's full natural range on the x-axis (0-1 for
  # accuracy, 1-9 for ratings), not just the range spanned by the data.
  # NOTE: `labels = NULL` in scale_x_continuous() means "no tick labels at
  # all" (not "use default labels") -- only pass `labels` when the caller
  # actually supplied custom ones, otherwise ggplot's default (derived
  # from `breaks`) is used.
  if (!is.null(xlim_range) || !is.null(xbreaks)) {
    if (!is.null(xlabels)) {
      p <- p + scale_x_continuous(limits = xlim_range, breaks = xbreaks, labels = xlabels)
    } else {
      p <- p + scale_x_continuous(limits = xlim_range, breaks = xbreaks)
    }
  }
  p
}
```

```{r}
#| label: trial-schematic-step2-model-intercepts-accuracy
#| include: false

re_acc <- brms::ranef(
  dev.all.studies.noratings.ptqs.normal.0.1.normal.0.1.lkj.2.study.ri,
  summary = TRUE
)
fixef_intercept_acc <- brms::fixef(
  dev.all.studies.noratings.ptqs.normal.0.1.normal.0.1.lkj.2.study.ri
)["Intercept", "Estimate"]

model_study       <- tibble(mean = plogis(fixef_intercept_acc + re_acc$study[, "Estimate", "Intercept"]))
model_participant <- tibble(mean = plogis(fixef_intercept_acc + re_acc$ResponseId[, "Estimate", "Intercept"]))
model_text        <- tibble(mean = plogis(fixef_intercept_acc + re_acc$text.id[, "Estimate", "Intercept"]))
model_question    <- tibble(mean = plogis(fixef_intercept_acc + re_acc$text.question.id[, "Estimate", "Intercept"]))

rm(re_acc); invisible(gc())

# -- the full accuracy fit is not needed again after this chunk; discard it
# now (per this project's convention of not holding multiple ~800MB brmsfit
# objects in memory simultaneously across a long combined render).
rm(dev.all.studies.noratings.ptqs.normal.0.1.normal.0.1.lkj.2.study.ri); invisible(gc())

fill_values_acc <- c("Raw mean" = "grey50", "Model estimate" = "limegreen")
```

```{r}
#| label: trial-schematic-step2-model-intercepts-ratings
#| include: false

re_rat <- brms::ranef(
  dev.ord.rating.all.studies.pts.normal.0.1.normal.0.1.lkj.2.study.ri.ad95,
  summary = TRUE
)
fixef_rat <- brms::fixef(dev.ord.rating.all.studies.pts.normal.0.1.normal.0.1.lkj.2.study.ri.ad95)
thresholds_rat <- fixef_rat[grepl("^Intercept\\[", rownames(fixef_rat)), "Estimate"]

expected_rating <- function(u, thresholds) {
  p_le <- outer(thresholds, u, function(th, uu) plogis(th - uu))
  1 + colSums(1 - p_le)
}

model_study_rat       <- tibble(mean = expected_rating(re_rat$study[, "Estimate", "Intercept"],      thresholds_rat))
model_participant_rat <- tibble(mean = expected_rating(re_rat$ResponseId[, "Estimate", "Intercept"], thresholds_rat))
model_text_rat        <- tibble(mean = expected_rating(re_rat$text.id[, "Estimate", "Intercept"],    thresholds_rat))

rm(re_rat); invisible(gc())

# -- likewise discard the full ratings fit now that its ranef()/fixef()
# summaries have been extracted.
rm(dev.ord.rating.all.studies.pts.normal.0.1.normal.0.1.lkj.2.study.ri.ad95); invisible(gc())

fill_values_rat <- c("Raw mean" = "grey50", "Model estimate" = "skyblue")
rat_breaks <- 1:9
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-composite-design-schema
#| fig-cap: "**The implications when we test the response of participants to questions about texts.**"
#| fig-width: 8.5
#| fig-height: 12
#| fig-pos: 'H'

library(magick)
library(grid)

qmd_base <- tryCatch(tools::file_path_sans_ext(knitr::current_input()), error = function(e) NA)
if (is.null(qmd_base) || is.na(qmd_base)) qmd_base <- "trial-design-schematic-figure-composite-only"
files_dir <- paste0(qmd_base, "_files")

find_chunk_image <- function(label_pattern) {
  candidates <- list.files(files_dir, pattern = label_pattern, recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)
  # -- prefer the vector PDF source over a PNG fallback, if both exist
  candidates[order(!grepl("\\.pdf$", candidates))][1]
}

schematic_path <- find_chunk_image("^fig-trial-schematic-diagrams-1\\.(pdf|png)$")
equation_path  <- find_chunk_image("^fig-trial-model-equation-composite-1\\.(pdf|png)$")

read_as_grob <- function(path, density = 300) {
  img <- if (grepl("\\.pdf$", path)) {
    magick::image_read_pdf(path, density = density)
  } else {
    magick::image_read(path)
  }
  # -- trim surrounding whitespace so each image's leftmost *content*
  # (here, always the panel label -- "(a.)"/"(c.)" sit at the leftmost
  # x-coordinate in their respective tikz pictures) lands at column 0 of
  # the raster. Since rasterGrob() below stretches to fill its patchwork
  # cell exactly, this makes the label's left edge coincide with the
  # panel's left edge, matching the (d.)/(e.) ggplot titles' left-aligned
  # text (see make_row_title()) instead of drifting per-image depending
  # on each tikz picture's own incidental bounding-box padding.
  img <- magick::image_trim(img)
  rasterGrob(as.raster(img), interpolate = TRUE)
}

schematic_grob <- read_as_grob(schematic_path)
equation_grob  <- read_as_grob(equation_path)

# -- a small text-only "panel" used as a shared title above each grid, in
# place of per-panel titles. An explicit finite 0-1 coordinate system
# (rather than x = -Inf on a scale-less empty ggplot, which did not
# reliably resolve) with hjust = 0 at x = 0 left-justifies the text at the
# left edge of this panel -- which spans the full composite width, same as
# the schematic/equation panels above.
make_row_title <- function(label) {
  ggplot() +
    # -- `expand = c(0, 0)` removes ggplot's default 5% axis expansion,
    # which otherwise inset x = 0 (and therefore the hjust = 0 label
    # below) away from this panel's true left edge -- that inset, plus
    # patchwork's default cross-panel axis alignment (fixed below at the
    # call site via `wrap_elements(full = ...)`), was the actual cause of
    # (d.)/(e.) appearing shifted right of the trimmed, left-anchored
    # (a.)/(c.) tikz labels, not a font/margin issue
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), expand = c(0, 0)) +
    # -- size chosen (and left margin zeroed) to match the trimmed,
    # left-anchored (a.)/(c.) tikz labels above as closely as a raster
    # image and vector ggplot text can be matched; confirmed by visual
    # comparison of the rendered composite, not derived analytically
    annotate("text", x = 0, y = 0.5, label = label, fontface = "bold", size = 5.2, hjust = 0) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(plot.margin = margin(t = 2, b = 2, l = 0, r = 2)) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off")
}

# -- x-axis label is now the grouping-factor name (panel_title = NULL
# suppresses the per-panel title used in the walkthrough); accuracy
# breaks are widened to 0.5 so labels show one decimal place (0.0/0.5/1.0)
acc_breaks_composite <- c(0, 0.5, 1)

p.acc.study.grid       <- make_overlay_hist(raw_study,       model_study,       fill_values_acc, xlab = "Study",       binwidth = 0.05, xlim_range = c(0, 1), xbreaks = acc_breaks_composite)
p.acc.participant.grid <- make_overlay_hist(raw_participant, model_participant, fill_values_acc, xlab = "Participant", binwidth = 0.05, xlim_range = c(0, 1), xbreaks = acc_breaks_composite)
p.acc.text.grid        <- make_overlay_hist(raw_text,        model_text,        fill_values_acc, xlab = "Text",        binwidth = 0.05, xlim_range = c(0, 1), xbreaks = acc_breaks_composite)
p.acc.question.grid    <- make_overlay_hist(raw_question,    model_question,    fill_values_acc, xlab = "Question",    binwidth = 0.05, xlim_range = c(0, 1), xbreaks = acc_breaks_composite)

p.rat.study.grid       <- make_overlay_hist(raw_study_rat,       model_study_rat,       fill_values_rat, xlab = "Study",       binwidth = 0.4, xlim_range = c(1, 9), xbreaks = rat_breaks)
p.rat.participant.grid <- make_overlay_hist(raw_participant_rat, model_participant_rat, fill_values_rat, xlab = "Participant", binwidth = 0.4, xlim_range = c(1, 9), xbreaks = rat_breaks)
p.rat.text.grid        <- make_overlay_hist(raw_text_rat,        model_text_rat,        fill_values_rat, xlab = "Text",        binwidth = 0.4, xlim_range = c(1, 9), xbreaks = rat_breaks)

# -- manual compact legend (not extracted from a real scale, since the
# accuracy and ratings panels use two different fill scales): three
# colour swatches stacked vertically (this cell is narrow but tall), each
# with its label printed above, not beside, the swatch
legend_key <- tibble(
  y = 3:1,
  colour = c("limegreen", "skyblue", "grey50"),
  label = c("Model estimate (accuracy)", "Model estimate (ratings)", "Raw mean")
)
p_legend <- ggplot(legend_key, aes(x = 0, y = y)) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = colour), width = 0.7, height = 0.5, colour = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = label, y = y + 0.42), size = 2.6, lineheight = 0.85) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  xlim(-1.6, 1.6) +
  ylim(0.3, 3.9) +
  theme_void()

# -- suppress each panel's own (ggplot-generated) legend since the manual
# legend above replaces it
row_acc <- (p.acc.study.grid + p.acc.participant.grid + p.acc.text.grid + p.acc.question.grid) +
  plot_layout(nrow = 1) &
  theme(legend.position = "none")
row_rat <- (p.rat.study.grid + p.rat.participant.grid + p.rat.text.grid + p_legend) +
  plot_layout(nrow = 1) &
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# -- all five composite labels are now produced by the identical
# make_row_title() helper (see its definition above), rather than three
# of them (a./b./c.) being baked into tikz rasters at a separately-tuned
# font size. (a.)/(b.) sit side by side (widths approximate the schematic
# image's own left/right column proportions, confirmed by eye against the
# rendered composite) rather than each spanning the full width like
# (c.)/(d.)/(e.).
label_ab <- (make_row_title("(a.) Single study") + make_row_title("(b.) A sample of studies")) +
  plot_layout(widths = c(0.65, 0.35))

# -- every label -- including the two-part (a.)/(b.) row above -- is
# wrapped in `wrap_elements(full = ...)`, exactly like the schematic/
# equation raster panels. Patchwork otherwise aligns every plain ggplot
# panel's *plot area* (not just its outer cell) across the whole
# composite so axes line up column-wise -- which shifted bare row-title
# panels right to match row_acc/row_rat's y-axis label width, undoing the
# left-justification set inside make_row_title(). `full = ...` opts a
# panel out of that alignment and simply fills its entire cell
# edge-to-edge, matching how the schematic/equation rasters are placed.
wrap_elements(full = label_ab) /
  wrap_elements(full = schematic_grob) /
  wrap_elements(full = make_row_title("(c.) Likelihood")) /
  wrap_elements(full = equation_grob) /
  wrap_elements(full = make_row_title("(d.) Response accuracy")) /
  row_acc /
  wrap_elements(full = make_row_title("(e.) Rated understanding")) /
  row_rat +
  plot_layout(heights = c(0.15, 3.3, 0.15, 1.15, 0.15, 1, 0.15, 1))
```
